valueTrapFlags: Earnings drifting down: Q3 operating profit -4% YoY, net profit -4%; net interest income YTD -1%; FY2025 EPS 1.39 below FY2024 1.44 and FY2023 1.37 roughly flat.
Net loan loss ratio was only 1bp in FY2025 (target ~10bp over time), so credit costs are a likely headwind.
ROE has slipped from 16.9% (2023) / 16.7% (2024) to ~15%, near the guidance floor.
Capital return (high payout and buybacks) holds EPS up; CET1 15.8% leaves 1.9pp buffer.

valuation.method: Bank: next-12m EPS x justified P/E. Basis SEK 14.6 = price 187.45 / agent trailing P/E 12.81 (derived; company reports in EUR). Dividend yield assumed from 65% payout policy x 7.8% earnings yield (estimate, FX unverified). Buybacks not included.
valuation.metricBasis: EPS SEK-equivalent, TTM (derived from agent P/E)

bear.note: Rate cuts compress net interest income, credit losses normalise. Justified multiple 10x on next-12m 13.72.

base.note: ROE about 15%, flat-ish earnings plus capital return. Justified multiple 12x on next-12m 14.89.

bull.note: Volume growth and cost efficiency keep ROE near 16%. Justified multiple 13.5x on next-12m 15.33.

valuation.whyItFits: Largest Nordic bank: ROE 15.1%, CET1 15.8%, cost/income 45%, about 5% dividend plus buybacks; beta 0.72.
valuation.growthDrivers: Capital return (dividend and buybacks), lending volume, cost efficiency.
valuation.saturation: P/E 12.8 near the top of what Nordic banks earned at peak rates; UBS says much upside is priced in (analyst opinion).
valuation.principalRisk: Falling interest rates and normalising loan losses (currently 1bp) reduce earnings; Q3 operating profit -4%.
